name: Tapentadol
meta: Schedule H – prescription only (controlled dispensing under state NDPS rules; verify
sections: White to off-white powder (hydrochloride), freely soluble in water.

Designed as a single molecule combining mu-opioid agonism and norepinephrine reuptake inhibition (MOR-NRI); ER approved for diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain in 2012. First approval/introduction: Developed by Grünenthal (late 1980s); US FDA 2008 (IR) and 2011 (ER).

Mu-opioid receptor agonist combined with norepinephrine reuptake inhibition in a single molecule; effective in nociceptive and neuropathic pain with less GI intolerance than classical opioids. Receptor / target profile: Full mu-opioid agonist (Ki 0.1 µM; ~50x lower affinity than morphine) and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (Ki 0.48 µM); minimal serotonergic activity.
Hepatic – mainly glucuronidation (~55%); minor CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6; no active metabolites
Summary: Bioavailability ~32% (first-pass); ER Tmax 3–6 h. ~20% protein bound. Glucuronidated (no active metabolites; not CYP2D6-dependent). Half-life ~5–6 h. Renally excreted.
Severe chronic pain requiring opioid analgesia (chronic low back pain, osteoarthritis)
ER: start 50 mg twice daily (12 h apart); titrate by 50 mg twice daily every 3 days
Usual range 100–250 mg twice daily; max 500 mg/day
Swallow whole; never crush, chew or dissolve
Moderate hepatic impairment: start 50 mg once daily
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Moderate: start 50 mg ER once daily, max 100 mg/day; severe: avoid.
Start at lower end; monitor sedation.
Significant respiratory depression; acute or severe bronchial asthma (unmonitored)
Use with or within 14 days of MAO inhibitors
Acute intoxication with alcohol, hypnotics, opioids
Life-threatening respiratory depression; risk with benzodiazepines/alcohol
ER tablets must be swallowed whole – never crushed or chewed
With or without food; no alcohol (ER dose dumping).
Respiratory status; sedation; misuse; bowel function.
Miosis, respiratory depression, coma, seizures, cardiovascular collapse. Naloxone; supportive care.
Buynak et al., 2010 – tapentadol ER effective in chronic low back pain with better GI tolerability than oxycodone.
Schwartz et al., 2011 – effective in painful diabetic neuropathy.
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
